provenance.method: gemini-3-pro-image through scripts/art/gemini-image.py at 2048 px square, with the canonical athlete attached to every call. A master (start), then the finish and the mid-sweep as edits of the master; seven calls in all, three used. build.py then sets the start drawing's station below the pulleys into every frame with the selected block moved to the ladder heights, shifts the violet to #7B72E9, clamps near-black to black, crops all three drawings the same and resamples them once to 1000x1200. Nothing was redrawn by hand.

findings: Three positions, not six: start (frames 1, 2, 6), mid-sweep (3, 5) and finish (4). A separate early sweep at about 30 degrees was asked for three times and came back at hip height each time, so it is not drawn.
The torso of frame 4 is turned more square-on to the camera than in frames 1 and 3, so the back widens as the arms come down.
The near upper arm is painted the lats' violet in frames 1 and 3 and lilac in frame 4; the triceps are not one consistent secondary colour. The core is not visible from behind.

The station below the pulleys is the start drawing's in every frame and the five-plate block is moved by script to the ladder's gaps; the 0.92 px per mm scale is the start drawing's own gap read as 100 mm, not a calibration.
The 2:1 compound pulley in the ladder is not drawn; one cable runs from the top of the block up the column.
In frame 4 the left handle is mostly hidden behind the hip and its cable runs in front of the body, out of sight; the handles finish at the hips and upper thighs rather than the front of the thighs.
The station's crossbar is cut off by the top edge of the frame; the pulleys are whole.
Frames 3 and 5 show mid-sweep, so their placard t values changed from 1 and 0 to 0.5; the cue words are unchanged.
No anchors or contacts were measured beyond the 0 px registration of the head, legs and trainers between the generated drawings.
No person has played the set in the app at phone size: only the automated six-frame player check and screenshots.
